knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")

This vignette walks through the **Nakato et al. (2026)** ratio-based Stage 1
estimator for cluster randomized trials (CRTs) of strategies that aim to
*both* improve reach into the target population *and* health outcomes among
those reached. The motivating setup, from the SAPPHIRE / Peer-led DCP HIV
prevention trials:

* A cluster-level intervention is intended to expand **risk screening** (an
  indicator `M`) and increase **uptake of biomedical prevention** (the
  outcome `Y2`).
* True HIV risk status `Y1*` is **observed only among those screened** —
  i.e., when `M = 1`. We work with the observed `Y1 = M * Y1*`.
* The target population is *persons with HIV risk* — but membership in that
  population is partially missing, mediated by the intervention itself.

Simply restricting to the screened biases estimates because screening
mediates the intervention effect. Restricting to the observed-eligible
(`Y1 = 1`) inherits the same problem. The Nakato Stage 1 estimator
sidesteps this with a ratio:

$$
Y^c \;=\; \frac{\mathbb{P}(Y_2 = 1)}{\mathbb{E}\!\bigl[\mathbb{P}(Y_1 = 1 \mid M = 1, W)\bigr]}
$$

where the numerator is the empirical proportion uptaking and the
denominator is a TMLE for the prevalence of risk in the target population,
computed *within each cluster*, adjusted for baseline (and optionally
time-varying) covariates. Stage 2 then runs the usual cluster-level TMLE
on these cluster endpoints.

## 1. Simulate one CRT

We use a condensed version of the Nakato (2026) DGP. Each cluster has
`~100` individuals; the intervention `A` increases the probability of
screening; the outcome `Y2 = 1` is possible only among the
screened-and-eligible.

```{r dgp}
library(TwoStageTMLE)
library(data.table)

set.seed(2026)

gen_cluster <- function(N, j) {
  UE1 <- rep(runif(1, -1, 1), N); UE2 <- rep(runif(1, -1, 1), N)
  E1 <- rep(rnorm(1, UE1[1], 0.5), N); E2 <- rep(rnorm(1, UE2[1], 0.5), N)
  W1 <- rnorm(N, 0, 0.5); W2 <- rnorm(N, 0, 0.5); W3 <- rbinom(N, 1, 0.5)
  pY1 <- plogis(0.5 + W1 + W2 - W3 + 0.25*E1 + 0.25*E2)
  data.table(id = j, E1 = E1, E2 = E2, W1 = W1, W2 = W2, W3 = W3,
             UE1 = UE1, UE2 = UE2, Y1_star = as.integer(runif(N) < pY1))
}

J <- 20
N_per <- 120
dat <- rbindlist(lapply(seq_len(J), function(j) gen_cluster(N_per, j)))

# Randomize intervention at the cluster level
A_per <- sample(c(rep(1L, J/2), rep(0L, J/2)))
dat[, A := A_per[id]]

# Screening: boosted by A
pM <- plogis(-0.5 + 0.6*dat$A + 0.5*dat$W1 + 0.4*dat$W2 -
              0.4*dat$A*dat$W3 + 0.4*(1-dat$A)*dat$W3 +
              0.1*dat$UE1 + 0.1*dat$UE2)
dat[, M := as.integer(runif(.N) < pM)]

# Observed risk indicator
dat[, Y1 := Y1_star * M]

# Outcome: only happens among screened-AND-eligible
pY2 <- plogis(0.2 + 0.1*dat$A + dat$W1 + 0.5*dat$W2 +
              2*dat$W3 + 0.2*dat$E1 + 0.2*dat$E2)
dat[, Y2 := ifelse(Y1_star == 1 & M == 1,
                   as.integer(runif(.N) < pY2),
                   0L)]

dat[, c("UE1", "UE2", "Y1_star") := NULL]
head(dat)
```

About **`r round(100 * mean(dat$M))`%** of individuals are screened;
**`r round(100 * mean(dat$Y2))`%** end up taking up prevention.

## 2. Stage 1 — the ratio endpoint per cluster

`stage1_mediated()` fits, within each cluster, an `ltmle()` for
`E[P(Y1 = 1 | M = 1, W)]` (the denominator) and pairs it with the
empirical mean of `Y2` (the numerator). The default Super Learner library
is `c("SL.mean", "SL.glm", "SL.gam")`, matching Nakato (2026).

```{r stage1}
s1 <- stage1_mediated(
  data = dat,
  ind_cov  = c("W1", "W2", "W3"),     # baseline covariates W
  clust_cov = c("E1", "E2"),          # cluster-level covariates
  sl_library = c("SL.mean", "SL.glm") # smaller library for vignette speed
)
s1[, .(id, A, E1, E2, screened, eligible, unadj, tmle)]
```

Each row is one cluster. The four candidate endpoints:

* `screened` — `P(Y2 | M = 1)`: biased; conditions on the post-treatment
  screening indicator.
* `eligible` — `P(Y2 | Y1 = 1)`: biased; conditions on the
  observed-eligible (a post-treatment, partly-missing variable).
* `unadj` — ratio with the empirical denominator `P(Y1 | M = 1)`.
* **`tmle`** — ratio with the TMLE-adjusted denominator. This is the
  recommended endpoint and is what the driver hands to Stage 2.

> **Time-varying covariates.** Box 1 of Balzer et al. defines the
> denominator as `E[P(Y1 = 1 | M = 1, W, L)]` — that is, adjusting on
> baseline `W` *and* time-varying covariates `L`. Pass both via `ind_cov`
> if you have them. In this vignette `L` is empty.

## 3. Stage 2 — cluster-level TMLE on the ratio endpoint

Stage 2 is identical to the foundational two-stage workflow — the
`stage1_mediated()` output drops straight into `stage2_tmle()`:

```{r stage2}
s2_in <- copy(s1)
s2_in[, Y := tmle]
s2_in <- add_weights(s2_in, target = "clust")

cand <- cand_adj(c("E1", "E2"))

est <- suppressWarnings(stage2_tmle(
  data = s2_in,
  goal = "RD", target = "clust", break_match = TRUE,
  do_data_adapt = TRUE,
  cand_q_adj = cand$cand_q_adj, cand_q_form = cand$cand_q_form,
  cand_g_adj = cand$cand_g_adj, cand_g_form = cand$cand_g_form,
  remove_pscore = TRUE
))
est[, .(est, ci_lo, ci_hi, se, pval, q_adj, g_adj)]
```

## 4. End-to-end driver

The same analysis in a single call:

```{r e2e, eval = FALSE}
out <- two_stage_tmle_mediated(
  data = dat,
  ind_cov  = c("W1", "W2", "W3"),
  clust_cov = c("E1", "E2"),
  sl_library = c("SL.mean", "SL.glm"),
  goal = "RD", target = "clust", break_match = TRUE,
  do_data_adapt = TRUE,
  cand_q_adj = cand$cand_q_adj, cand_q_form = cand$cand_q_form,
  cand_g_adj = cand$cand_g_adj, cand_g_form = cand$cand_g_form,
  remove_pscore = TRUE
)
out$est         # Stage 2 estimate
out$stage1      # cluster table with screened/eligible/unadj/tmle endpoints
```

## 5. A note on variance

Stage 2's variance uses the cluster-level influence curve and **treats the
Stage 1 ratio `Yc` as a fixed observation at the cluster level**. The
Stage-1 contribution to overall variance is asymptotically negligible
when within-cluster sample sizes are large — see Box 2 of Balzer et al.
(2021). Nakato (2026) verifies acceptable coverage by simulation at
realistic cluster sizes (`N ≈ 200` per cluster, `J ∈ {20, 30, 50, 70}`).

For inference that is also robust to the Adaptive Pre-specification
selection, pass `do_cv_variance = TRUE` to `stage2_tmle()` (or via `...` in
the driver) — the returned data.table will have additional `cv_*` columns
with the CV-based CI and p-value.

## References

Nakato J., Balzer L.B. (2026). Methods for evaluating overall effectiveness
of cluster-level strategies aiming to improve reach and health outcomes.

Balzer L.B. et al. (2021). **Two-Stage TMLE to Reduce Bias and Improve
Efficiency in Cluster Randomized Trials.** arXiv:2106.15737.

Benitez A. et al. (2023). **Comparative methods for the analysis of cluster
randomized trials.** arXiv:2110.09633.
